source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: A blood collection under the scalp that does not cross sutures and resolves in weeks is:
questions.rationale: Cephalhematoma is subperiosteal blood that does not cross sutures and is absorbed in 3–6 weeks.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Newborn Head (PDF p. 219)
questions.quote: Absorbed within 3-6 weeks

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Until what age is strabismus considered normal?
questions.rationale: Strabismus is normal until about 6 months.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Newborn Eyes (PDF p. 219)
questions.quote: Strabismus is normal until 6 mos

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Low-set ears in a newborn may suggest:
questions.rationale: Low-set ears suggest chromosomal disorders such as trisomy 21 or kidney anomalies.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Newborn Ears (PDF p. 219)
questions.quote: The low set ears indicate Chromosomal disease such as

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How does the nurse test a newborn for choanal atresia?
questions.rationale: Close the mouth and occlude each naris to check for distress; inability to pass a catheter confirms it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Newborn Nose (PDF p. 220)
questions.quote: Test for CHOANAL ATRESIA (blockage at the rear of the nose) by closing the newborn’s mouth

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn's abdomen looks scaphoid (sunken). This suggests:
questions.rationale: An empty or scaphoid abdomen suggests missing contents, as in diaphragmatic hernia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Newborn Abdomen (PDF p. 220)
questions.quote: The abdomen of the child should look slightly protuberant

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: When does the umbilical cord usually fall off?
questions.rationale: The stump usually separates by day 6 to 10.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Umbilical Cord (PDF p. 220)
questions.quote: Umbilical cord should break free by day 6 to 10

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn has not passed meconium in 24 hours. What should be suspected?
questions.rationale: Failure to pass meconium in 24 hours suggests imperforate anus or meconium ileus.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anogenital Area (PDF p. 220)
questions.quote: If a newborn does not do so in the first 24 hours, suspect imperforate anus or meconium ileus

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: A female newborn has a blood-tinged vaginal discharge. This is:
questions.rationale: Maternal hormones cause pseudomenstruation and vulvar swelling, which are normal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Female Genitalia (PDF p. 220)
questions.quote: Pseudomenstruation

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A urethral opening on the underside of the penis is:
questions.rationale: Hypospadias is a ventral opening; epispadias is dorsal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Male Genitalia (PDF p. 220)
questions.quote: on the dorsal surface (epispadias)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A single transverse palmar crease suggests:
questions.rationale: A simian crease could signify Down syndrome.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Extremities (PDF p. 221)
questions.quote: Inspect the palm for a simian crease which could signify down syndrome

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A feeding tube cannot be passed into a newborn's stomach. This confirms:
questions.rationale: Failure to pass through the nares indicates choanal atresia; failure to reach the stomach indicates esophageal atresia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Congenital Anomaly Appraisal (PDF p. 221)
questions.quote: Failure to pass it into the stomach confirms presence of esophageal atresia

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Why should parents not prop the baby's bottle?
questions.rationale: Propping increases aspiration and otitis media risk and deprives infants of being held.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Breastfeeding Facts (PDF p. 221)
questions.quote: Caution parents not to prop bottles, because it increases the risk for aspiration and otitis media

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Why is warming formula in a microwave discouraged?
options: The inner core can get very hot
questions.rationale: Microwaving heats unevenly; the inner core may grow very hot and burn the infant.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Breastfeeding Facts (PDF p. 221)
questions.quote: the inner core of milk may grow very hot

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which is the most severe form of spina bifida?
questions.rationale: Myelomeningocele contains meninges, CSF, and spinal cord or nerves.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Spina Bifida (PDF p. 221)
questions.quote: It is the most severe form

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How is a newborn with myelomeningocele positioned before surgery?
questions.rationale: Prone positioning minimizes tension and trauma to the sac, which is covered with moist sterile nonadherent dressing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Spina Bifida (PDF p. 222)
questions.quote: Place in a prone position to minimize tension on the sac

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Before Birth
questions.stem: Which supplement helps prevent neural tube defects?
questions.rationale: Folic acid supplementation, especially in the first trimester, helps prevent neural tube defects.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Spina Bifida Prevention (PDF p. 222)
questions.quote: Pregnant women are advised to ingest 600 micrograms of folic acid daily

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 'cracked pot' sound on percussion of an infant's skull suggests:
questions.rationale: Macewen's sign in hydrocephalus results from widely separated skull bones.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hydrocephalus (PDF p. 222)
questions.quote: (Macewen’s sign) Bones of the head are widely separated that produces a cracked pot sound

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which shunt is most commonly used for hydrocephalus in children?
questions.rationale: The VP shunt connecting the lateral ventricle to the peritoneum is most common.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hydrocephalus (PDF p. 222)
questions.quote: Most commonly used shunt in children

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After VP shunt insertion, how is the child positioned?
questions.rationale: Position on the unoperated side to avoid pressure on the valve, flat to avoid rapid CSF reduction.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hydrocephalus (PDF p. 223)
questions.quote: Position the child on the unoperated side to prevent pressure on the shunt valve

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: What is the FIRST nursing action when an infant is admitted with bacterial meningitis?
questions.rationale: Isolation is the first action on admission; contacts may need prophylaxis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bacterial Meningitis (PDF p. 223)
questions.quote: Isolate infant: first nursing implementation on admission

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which CSF finding supports bacterial meningitis?
questions.rationale: Bacterial meningitis CSF is cloudy with increased protein and decreased glucose.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bacterial Meningitis (PDF p. 223)
questions.quote: Clouding of CSF, Increased Protein and Decreased Glucose

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with CP has a scissor-like gait. Which type is this?
questions.rationale: Spastic CP (cortex) is most common, with a scissor gait; athetoid involves basal ganglia; ataxic the cerebellum.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cerebral Palsy (PDF p. 224)
questions.quote: Spastic (most common): The cortex is affected resulting in the child having a scissor-like gait

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: White specks in the iris of a child with Down syndrome are:
questions.rationale: Brushfield spots are white iris specks seen in Down syndrome.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Down Syndrome (PDF p. 224)
questions.quote: Brushfield’s spots – white specks in the iris of the eye

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Care for a child with Down syndrome is planned according to:
questions.rationale: Treatment is based on developmental rather than chronological age.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Down Syndrome (PDF p. 225)
questions.quote: Treatment is based on the child’s developmental age rather than chronological age

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A continuous 'machinery' murmur suggests:
questions.rationale: PDA has a machinery-like murmur; VSD has a loud systolic murmur.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acyanotic Heart Defects (PDF p. 225)
questions.quote: Machinery like murmur – PDA

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which is the most common congenital heart defect?
questions.rationale: VSD is the most common CHD (about 30%), usually a left-to-right shunt.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, VSD (PDF p. 225)
questions.quote: Most common CHD: 30%

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant with a heart defect sweats on the scalp during feeding. This indicates:
questions.rationale: Brow or scalp sweating with feeding reflects fatigue and heart failure risk in CHD.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acyanotic Defects (PDF p. 225)
questions.quote: Easy fatigability shown as brow sweating (during feeding or crying episodes)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: What is the most common complication of acyanotic heart defects?
questions.rationale: CHF is the most common complication of acyanotic defects.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acyanotic Defects (PDF p. 225)
questions.quote: Congestive Heart Failure most common complication
